ai-at-work.title: AI agent startup LangChain hits $3B valuation
ai-at-work.excerpt: LangChain now claims 7,000 customers of its model and platform agnostic agent management tool LangSmith.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: LangChain, a startup building tools for managing AI agents across different platforms, just hit a $3 billion valuation with 7,000 paying customers on its LangSmith product. This matters because digital workplace teams are scrambling to integrate AI into their workflows, and standardized agent management platforms could become as essential as identity systems or collaboration hubs. The real test is whether LangChain becomes the plumbing layer everyone needs or another VC darling that fails to survive contact with enterprise reality.

ai-at-work.title: ElevenLabs’ new app combines meeting note-taking and dictation for teams
ai-at-work.excerpt: ElevenAI is a new meeting notetaker and dictation app aimed at teams and enterprises.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: ElevenLabs launched ElevenAI, a new app that combines meeting transcription and note-taking for team collaboration. This matters because most organizations are still drowning in meeting recordings nobody watches, so anything that actually captures and organizes what was said has real practical value. The honest take: we've been promised the perfect meeting app for a decade now, so I'll believe this one changes behavior when I see adoption numbers that don't look like a fitness tracker graveyard.

ai-at-work.title: FAA grounds all domestic flights after reported network outage
ai-at-work.excerpt: The Federal Aviation Administration today grounded all domestic flights in the U.S. The rare order was issued by the Air Traffic Control System Command Center, or ATCSCC. It’s an FAA facility in North
ai-at-work.dwp_take: The FAA grounded all domestic U.S. flights after a network outage at their Air Traffic Control System Command Center in Virginia. This matters to digital workplace pros because it's a brutal reminder that when critical infrastructure depends on systems without proper redundancy, everyone pays the price. If the FAA with unlimited budgets can't keep their network up, maybe we should all stop pretending our Slack integration is mission critical.

ai-at-work.title: NiCE’s next-generation Cognigy bets the hard part of AI agents is running them, not building them
ai-at-work.excerpt: The contact center has been the low-hanging fruit for the artificial intelligence industry. Ask any information technology or business leader what they want to use agentic AI for, and they will say it
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Cognigy is betting that the real challenge with AI agents isn't building them anymore, it's keeping them running reliably in production. For digital workplace folks handling employee experience and support operations, this matters because we've all watched flashy AI demos crash and burn in real deployments. If they're right that operations is the bottleneck, then knowing how to manage and monitor these systems becomes more valuable than having the latest LLM under the hood, which is refreshingly honest about AI's actual challenge.

tools-tech.title: Microsoft 365 services slowly come back online after global outage
tools-tech.excerpt: After a lengthy Microsoft 365 outage disrupted business around the globe, Microsoft is now restoring services to its customers. As of 6:00 p.m. UTC (1 p.m. ET) on Friday, Nov. 13, Microsoft said that
tools-tech.dwp_take: Microsoft 365 went down globally and took hours to come back up, with Exchange Online still limping along afterward. For digital workplace pros, this is a stark reminder that cloud dependency means you're one bad update away from your entire organization grinding to a halt, no matter how much you've invested in modern infrastructure. After thirty years in this space, I can tell you this never gets old: companies still don't have proper offline protocols, and that's exactly when you find out who actually runs your business.

tools-tech.title: Microsoft 365 caught a bug and the whole world sneezed
tools-tech.excerpt: While Microsoft seems at last to be on the edge of fixing the global outage that hammered its services overnight, causing chaos across Asia-Pacific and Europe, we should still ask: How many times must
tools-tech.dwp_take: Microsoft 365 went down hard overnight, affecting services across Asia-Pacific and Europe and causing real disruption for organizations relying entirely on their stack. For digital workplace leaders, this is the millionth reminder that single-vendor dependency is a business continuity disaster waiting to happen, yet somehow we keep doing it anyway. Look, I've seen this movie before, and the ending never changes: companies will spend two weeks panicking, a month planning, and then go right back to betting the farm on one cloud provider because it's cheaper and easier than maintaining a hybrid setup.

tools-tech.title: For November, Patch Tuesday means a to-do list that starts with Outlook
tools-tech.excerpt: November is a (relatively) big month. Microsoft’s November 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes 1,240 CVEs, 64 of them rated critical. Start with Outlook: attackers are already using CVE-2026-124194, a spoofing f
tools-tech.dwp_take: Microsoft just dropped patches for 1,240 vulnerabilities this November, with 64 critical ones including an actively exploited Outlook spoofing flaw that attackers are already weaponizing. For IT teams managing digital workplaces, this means prioritization is everything because you can't patch everything at once and some of these gaps are actively being exploited right now. After three decades watching patch cycles, I'll say it plainly: the fact that Outlook is the first target tells you everything about why email security deserves to be your number one priority, not your number five.

tools-tech.title: US tech jobs grow in a ‘low-hire, low-fire’ market
tools-tech.excerpt: Tech jobs grew in October, and the holiday season will provide a boost in an otherwise “low-hire, low-fire” market, data released by research firms showed. The tech industry added 7,200 jobs, and tech
tools-tech.dwp_take: Tech hiring stayed modest in October with just 7,200 new jobs added to the tech sector, though broader tech roles across industries hit 26,000. For digital workplace pros, this slow-growth environment means your current gig is probably safer but advancement opportunities are fewer, so you'd better be good at what you do. The "low-hire, low-fire" label is corporate speak for "they're keeping who they've got and being stingy with new headcount," which honestly beats the layoff rollercoaster we've seen lately.

digital-culture.title: A remote employee refused 160 webcam photos a day. Her employer fired her
digital-culture.excerpt: Across the workforce, employer surveillance is growing increasingly common, even though it is widely disliked by employees. According to the American Psychological Association, employee monitoring inc
digital-culture.dwp_take: A company fired a remote worker for refusing to submit to 160 webcam photos per day, which the employer justified as productivity monitoring. This matters because digital workplace leaders are caught between wanting accountability and driving talent away with invasive surveillance that actually tanks morale and performance. Look, if you need 160 photos a day to know someone's working, the real problem isn't the employee's camera.

digital-culture.title: Microsoft’s massive outage puts its AI-driven layoffs under scrutiny
digital-culture.excerpt: Microsoft’s massive service outage on Thursday left businesses and government agencies scrambling to access critical services. It also came at an awkward moment for the tech giant, which has undertake
digital-culture.dwp_take: Microsoft's global outage knocked out critical services for businesses and government agencies just as the company was aggressively laying off workers while simultaneously investing billions in AI. This matters because digital workplace leaders are watching to see whether AI-driven cost cutting actually leaves organizations more resilient or just more fragile when systems fail. Here's the uncomfortable truth: you can't automate your way out of needing competent people to keep the lights on, and this outage is a pretty expensive reminder of that lesson.

digital-culture.title: The hidden cost of workplace transformation: How change initiatives crush top employees
digital-culture.excerpt: Nearly half of employees report experiencing "transformation fatigue," according to a recent study
digital-culture.dwp_take: So half your workforce is burned out from constant change initiatives. That's not a feature of transformation, that's a bug you paid consultants six figures to install. Digital workplace leaders need to understand that every new tool, process redesign, and "strategic pivot" has a real human cost in productivity and morale. Here's the truth nobody wants to hear: you don't need another transformation program, you need to let the last one actually work for six months.

digital-culture.title: ‘Bah, humbug!’ Could employee apathy mean curtains for the traditional holiday party?
digital-culture.excerpt: People say they prefer cash or time off, though some argue office gatherings are still beneficial
digital-culture.dwp_take: Companies are discovering that traditional holiday parties don't move the needle anymore because employees would rather have cash bonuses or extra PTO than attend another forced-fun event. This matters because it signals a fundamental shift in how we think about workplace culture, connection, and what actually motivates people in the post-pandemic world. Here's my take: if your holiday party needs a motivational speech to get butts in seats, you're doing culture wrong, and honestly, you probably should just give people the money.

industry-news.title: FAA Grounds US Flights Nationwide, Citing ‘Extraordinary’ Safety Concerns
industry-news.excerpt: FAA grounds flights nationwide, citing extraordinary safety concerns amid air traffic control communications problems. Here's what travelers need to know. The post FAA Grounds US Flights Nationwide, C
industry-news.dwp_take: The FAA grounded all US flights due to critical failures in air traffic control communications systems. This is a stark reminder that the digital infrastructure keeping mission-critical operations running needs redundancy, testing, and honest assessment of aging systems. If your organization's digital workplace infrastructure is held together with the same level of prayer and duct tape as apparently some of our nation's air traffic control systems, now would be a very good time to have that conversation with your IT leadership.

industry-news.title: Toshiba Wins UK Contract to Scale Quantum Networks With BT, Colt
industry-news.excerpt: Toshiba Europe won an Innovate UK contract to build long-distance, multi-user quantum network subsystems, with BT and Colt testing them on real fiber. The post Toshiba Wins UK Contract to Scale Quantu
industry-news.dwp_take: Toshiba Europe just landed UK government funding to develop quantum network technology that BT and Colt will test on actual fiber infrastructure. For digital workplace folks, this matters because quantum networks could eventually deliver the kind of security and speed that makes today's concerns about data breaches look quaint. That said, we're probably a decade away from this affecting your Slack performance, so don't panic about needing quantum-ready office tech just yet.

industry-news.title: Samsung and Google Open AI Glasses Preorders: What $395 Gets You
industry-news.excerpt: Samsung and Google open AI glasses preorders from $395. Explore Gemini features, Warby Parker and Gentle Monster styles, release dates, and phone compatibility. The post Samsung and Google Open AI Gla
industry-news.dwp_take: Samsung and Google are taking preorders for AI-powered glasses starting at $395, featuring Google's Gemini assistant and available through Warby Parker and Gentle Monster frames. For digital workplace folks, this matters because wearable AI is creeping closer to becoming an actual work tool rather than a sci-fi concept, which means we need to start thinking about policies and use cases now. Honestly, I'll believe it's a real productivity game-changer when I see people actually wearing these in meetings instead of just talking about them at conferences.

industry-news.title: Apple Wants $50 for More AI Usage: How Much Do You Actually Get?
industry-news.excerpt: Apple now sells $49.99 AI usage packs for Creator Studio subscribers. Here's how they work, who qualifies, and why the extra capacity is hard to predict. The post Apple Wants $50 for More AI Usage: Ho
industry-news.dwp_take: Apple is charging $50 for expanded AI usage packs within Creator Studio, though the actual capacity you'll get remains murky. This matters because it signals how vendors are starting to meter and monetize AI features separately, which will affect how IT teams budget for creative tools and manage user expectations. Honestly, charging extra for undefined AI capacity feels like selling someone a bigger bucket without telling them how many gallons it holds, which tracks for Apple's pricing philosophy but seems destined to frustrate the professionals footing the bill.
